retained_structural_inputs.statement: Actual closed rank-one zero-section and first jet give B->R/(f) surjective.
One-place primitive polynomials have integral reduced levels; generic genus equals normalization genus plus finite deficit.
Complete isomorphic inverse image of one one-place target curve forces Keller inverse.
Exact boundary defect retains finite-image punctures and gives the normalized component loss formula.
Square-free Keller pullbacks, divisor domination and quasi-finiteness.
Etale base change preserves normality, retained Stacks025P.

direct_proof_arguments: The target image ideal has no embedded primes because its quotient is a Cohen-Macaulay plane hypersurface ring; primary localization in a UFD makes it principal.
The actual source divisor is a section over the target image; the open-and-closed section theorem makes a(K)=f g with (f,g)=1, including multiplicities.
Every extra prime over a selected radical component is disjoint from that component and from the whole radical curve by its closed injectivity.
Units on a one-place curve are constant, so two disjoint one-place plane curves have affine-related defining equations by degree comparison.
If every pullback component were one-place, b(K) would be a nonlinear composition in p, contradicting its finite critical locus from the Keller differential and reduced one-place target levels.
A forced multi-puncture component has p as a nonconstant unit; a constant restriction would make it an integral one-place p-level.
Etale normalization and the one-puncture boundary formula make each one-place component over an A1-normalized target degree one with normalization A1.
Intrinsic equal pencil genus gives equal normalization deficits, so those finite birational component maps are actual isomorphisms.
The complete one-place Milnor budget bounds the number of such isomorphic levels by 2 delta/(2 delta minus branch defect), at most two.
Equality delta=branch defect forces ordinary nodes by the completed normalization ring and its plane embedding dimension.
Every forced multiple-puncture component over target normalization A1 has finite-image boundary index E=e+2g-2+r at least e.
